summary:
Project Summary: AeroMed Astronaut Health & Diagnostic Workstation

What We Developed:
AeroMed is an autonomous, flight-grade clinical and laboratory diagnostic workstation engineered for deep-space missions. Powered by a Python FastAPI backend and a responsive React telemetry dashboard, AeroMed integrates multi-modal physiological sensing (AD8232 ECG, MAX30102 PPG, cuffless PAT blood pressure, sEMG dynamometry), point-of-care ultrasound/FibroScan imaging, and comprehensive onboard laboratory diagnostics—including a dedicated immune monitoring module supporting 5-part CBC hematology, flow cytometry, and cytokine ELISA multiplexing.

How It Addresses the Challenge:
Long-duration interplanetary travel entails severe communication latencies and blackout windows that prevent reliance on Earth-based medical teams. AeroMed solves this by executing edge-computed signal parsing, automated quality control, and longitudinal baseline drift analysis locally on spacecraft hardware, delivering immediate clinical decision support without requiring terrestrial cloud connectivity.

Why It Is Important:
Prolonged microgravity and space radiation trigger progressive cardiovascular deconditioning, muscular atrophy, and immune dysregulation. By providing continuous, non-invasive biomarker surveillance and trend alerts, AeroMed enables autonomous, early detection of subclinical physiological deterioration, empowering crews to deploy timely countermeasures and ensure mission survival.
details:
AeroMed is an edge-computed, kiosk-grade clinical and diagnostic workstation designed for human spaceflight crews. It functions as an autonomous, onboard medical bay that continuously acquires, validates, and interprets physiological signals and laboratory assays:

  • Physiological Telemetry & Hemodynamics: Interfaces with an AD8232 ECG front-end (Lead-II vector) and a MAX30102 dual-wavelength optical sensor (660nm Red / 880nm IR PPG). An onboard fusion algorithm calculates Pulse Arrival Time (PAT)—measuring the latency between the ventricular electrical depolarization (ECG R-peak) and the peripheral arterial pressure pulse arrival—to provide continuous, cuffless blood pressure estimates alongside SpO2SpO_2SpO2​ and heart rate.
    1. 5-Part Differential Hematology Analyzer: Measures total WBC, neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils.
    2. Flow Cytometer: Multi-laser PMT immunophenotyping tracking CD3+, CD4+ helper, CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, CD19+ B cells, CD16/56+ NK cells, and the critical CD4/CD8 ratio.
    3. ELISA Microplate Reader: Dual-wavelength (450nm/630nm) photometric evaluation calculating standard-curve optical densities for inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-10, TNF-α\alphaα, IFN-γ\gammaγ, IL-2) and immunoglobulins (IgG, IgA, IgM).
  • Deterministic Decision Support: All telemetry and lab results are evaluated against individual astronaut baseline bands and clinical reference intervals, surfacing longitudinal trend alerts and automated mission summaries without needing internet connectivity.

    Benifits Include:
  • Zero Cloud Dependency: Operates 100% offline at the spacecraft edge, eliminating vulnerability to transmission dropouts, bandwidth constraints, and orbital blackout zones.
  • Unified Single-Screen Workstation: Replaces disjointed, single-purpose medical gadgets with a single coherent dashboard, dramatically decreasing the crew’s cognitive burden and setup time.
  • Early Detection of Subclinical Degradation: Rather than waiting for acute symptoms to manifest, the system tracks subtle longitudinal shifts (e.g., progressive CD4/CD8 ratio inversion, baseline heart-rate variability decay, or muscle force attenuation).
  • Strict Data Integrity & Quality Control: The system enforces rigorous biomedical validation—preventing unverified optical density readings from being treated as biomarker concentrations, barring absolute cell count estimations without validated lymphocyte counts, and prominently watermarking simulated vs. physical hardware telemetry.

    Impact:
  • Human Deep-Space Exploration: As humanity ventures to the Moon (Artemis program) and onward to Mars, round-trip radio communication delays reach up to 44 minutes, rendering terrestrial telemedicine impossible during emergencies. AeroMed provides the autonomy required to keep crews medically self-reliant and mission-capable.
  • Terrestrial Remote Medicine: Beyond spaceflight, the exact same system architecture directly addresses acute medical challenges on Earth: Antarctic research stations, naval submarines, offshore drilling rigs, combat field hospitals, and underserved rural clinics that face identical constraints of medical isolation and zero connectivity.

    Tools,Language and Hardware:
    • AD8232 Single-Lead Heart Rate Monitor Analog Front-End.
    • MAX30102 High-Sensitivity Pulse Oximeter & Heart-Rate Sensor.
    • HX711 24-bit ADC Wheatstone-bridge load-cell amplifier + Ag/AgCl surface electrodes.
    • 3.5 MHz broadband phased-array acoustic piezoelectric ultrasound probe.
    • 50 Hz mechanical shear-wave piston actuator with 3.5 MHz A-mode tracking transceiver (VCTE).
    • 488nm (FITC/PE) & 638nm (APC) multi-laser photomultiplier tubes (Flow Cytometer).
    • 450nm measurement / 630nm reference dual-wavelength photometric filter wheel (ELISA).

      How is my project creative?
    • Multi-Modal Hemodynamic Fusion: Instead of relying on a bulky, power-hungry inflatable pneumatic arm cuff, AeroMed mathematically fuses the electrical vector from the AD8232 ECG with the peripheral optical waveform from the MAX30102 PPG to derive cuffless, continuous blood pressure via Pulse Arrival Time (PAT).
    • Individualized Astronaut Baseline Modeling: Standard clinical tools compare individuals to broad population averages. AeroMed models each astronaut's personal pre-flight baseline and flags relative trajectory drift—essential for detecting spaceflight-specific degradation like radiation-induced lymphopenia or microgravity fluid shift.
    • Human-Centered Medical UI: Rather than looking like a generic template, the interface is styled as a purpose-built aerospace clinical monitor: featuring dark high-contrast glanceability, explicit input transducer specifications on every scan, categorized alert severity, and intuitive hardware connection controls.

      Factors my team considered
    • Spaceflight Environmental Constraints: Considered microgravity cephalad fluid shifts, cosmic ionizing radiation, bone demineralization, and muscular atrophy, selecting diagnostic modalities that specifically target these known risks.
    • Medical Ethics & Decision Boundaries: Designed the intelligence engine to detect trends, validate quality control, and explain anomalies without attempting black-box clinical diagnoses or unverified radiation-injury claims.
    • Hardware Interoperability & Extensibility: Acknowledged that spaceflight instruments do not share uniform communication protocols by implementing an extensible Adapter Pattern (CBCAnalyzerAdapter, FlowCytometerAdapter, ELISAReaderAdapter, HardwareManager) that supports both simulated testing streams and physical serial/USB device integration.
    • Fail-Safe Operation & Resilience: Engineered deterministic fallbacks so that if a single sensor channel disconnects or drops packets, the remaining independent diagnostic modules continue functioning without crashing the workstation.
